To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the latencies and the amplitudes of P1 and Nl are predicted by phase synchronization between oscillations of different frequencies.

(1) evoked oscillatory responses undergo significant phase resetting and synchronization in a memory retrieval task; (2) phase synchronization occurs in a time window that is consistent with the latency of the P1 and N2 components; and (3) the phase synchronization is stronger between frequencies that are closer in the frequency domain.
(i) phase synchronization in the alpha band is a good predictor of ERP latencies and amplitudes and that (ii) this synchronization occurs in the same time windows as the P1 and N2 complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the P1-N2 complex is generated by phase resetting of oscillations.
the question how the human brain processes information.
the question of whether and how oscillatory brain activity is involved in the generation of event-related potential (ERPs) components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phase resetting and phase synchronization are important for understanding the generation of the P1 and N2 components of the visual ERP.
phase synchronization between frequencies predicts the latencies of P1 and N2, and that the amplitude of the P1 is predicted by phase synchronization between alpha and delta.
phase resetting and phase synchronization are two different aspects of the same process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alpha phase synchronization predicts P100 and N100 latency and amplitude size.
the phase-resetting model of ERP generation is supported by the present data.
alpha phase synchronization is a key mechanism in memory retrieval and that alpha phase resetting predicts the P1 and N2 amplitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phase synchronization between frequencies can be a useful tool to understand the neural mechanisms of ERP generation.
phase synchronization is not only a mechanism for information transfer but can also explain the latency and amplitude of ERP components.
the phase-resetting model can account for the latencies and amplitudes of P1-N1 components.
